UserProfile.title: User Profile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile information, linking them to a company and role.

companyId.description: The ID of the company the user belongs to.

role.description: The user's role within the company.

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the user profile was created.

isPaid.description: Indicates if the user's subscription is active.

status.description: The status of the user account.

Company.title: Company
Company.description: Represents a company or organization using the application.

ownerId.description: The UID of the user who created and owns the company account.

userCount.description: The number of users expected to use the application for this company.

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the company was created.

Product.title: Product
Product.description: Represents a product in the inventory.

quantityAvailable.description: Quantity of the product currently available in stock.

warehouseLocation.description: Location of the product in the warehouse.

quantity.description: Quantity of the product sold in this transaction.

salePrice.description: Price at which the product was sold.

paymentType.description: Type of payment used for the sale (cash, partial, loan).

saleDate.description: Date when the sale was made.

Client.title: Client
Client.description: Represents a client who purchases products.

ClientLoan.title: ClientLoan
ClientLoan.description: Represents a loan issued to a client.

loanAmount.description: Amount of the loan issued to the client.

loanIssueDate.description: Date when the loan was issued.

dueDate.description: Date when the loan is due.

amountPaid.description: Amount that the client has paid towards the loan.

factoryName.description: Name of the factory associated with the supplier.

SupplierPayment.title: SupplierPayment
SupplierPayment.description: Represents a payment made to a supplier.

payableAmount.description: Total amount payable to the supplier.

remainingBalance.description: Remaining balance to be paid to the supplier.

paymentDate.description: Date when the payment was made.

InventoryLog.title: InventoryLog
InventoryLog.description: Represents a log entry for inventory changes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the inventory log.

changeQuantity.description: The amount that the inventory has changed

logDate.description: Date when the change to inventory was recorded.

Currency.title: Currency
Currency.description: Represents a currency supported by the system.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to support FlowVia's requirements for warehouse, sales, financing, and multi-currency management. The design prioritizes authorization independence, clarity, and scalability. It leverages path-based ownership for user-related data and membership maps for collaborative data access.

Authorization Independence is achieved through denormalization.  For instance, while not explicitly required by the current schema, if sales records needed to be restricted to specific users, the user's ID or relevant role information would be denormalized directly into the `sales` documents to avoid using `get()` calls in security rules.  Similar denormalization strategies would apply to other entities if access control requires information from related entities.

QAPs (Rules are not Filters) are supported by segregating data based on access requirements. Path-based ownership (`/clients/{clientId}/clientLoans/{clientLoanId}`) naturally provides secure `list` operations for a client's own loans. Membership Maps would be used if collaborative access was later required, ensuring that listing operations could be secured by checking for membership in the appropriate map within the listed documents.

The structure uses explicit state modeling (though the current data entities don't explicitly define a 'status' field, a `status` field should be added to relevant entities where state management is needed) and predictable schema to enhance debuggability. Standardized naming conventions are applied across all paths and fields.
